title: Shadow Load Gating — Weekly Performance Sync 2026-11-05
body:
Attendees: Anika, Diego, Priya, Samir, Tess. Duration: 45m. Primary focus: investigate throughput drop observed in shadow load gating experiments (mixed interleaved+single-turn traffic) across the new gating policy deployed to the canary fleet on 2026-11-02.

Summary of observations:
- Symptom: sustained ~18-25% end-to-end throughput regression on canary under synthetic mixed-client traffic when gating is enabled, but median latency remained similar. Regression surfaced first in shadow-run logs (shadow-run-2026-11-03) and later reproduced in controlled lab.
- Key metrics that regressed: overall tokens/sec down 20%, p95 latency unchanged, p99 increased from 310ms -> 380ms for the interleaved-seq workload. CPU on the host remained under 70% but GPU SM utilization dropped ~10 percentage points during the regression window.
- Notably, queue length at the request router spiked intermittently (max queue depth +40) and correlated with short-lived bursts of KV-cache evictions measured by cache-metrics (kv_evict_rate up).

Hypothesis and root-cause threading:
- Primary hypothesis: gating policy introduces per-model admission checks that occasionally serialize requests for model-switching paths. When an interleaved sequence stream causes frequent model switching + cold KV-cache entries, admission gating locks a per-model token bucket while KV cache rebuilds, causing head-of-line blocking for other requests destined for the same model shard. This produces lower GPU occupancy (explains SM drop) and increased p99 for affected traces.
- Secondary hypothesis: the gating handler invokes the model-variant validation flow which triggers a synchronous metadata fetch (small RPC to model-store) on the hot path; occasional latency on that RPC cascades into queueing backpressure.

What we ran in lab (tests & results):
1) Shadow-run replay A: baseline traffic (gating disabled) — tokens/sec 120k, queue depth 95th=2, p99=310ms.
2) Shadow-run replay B: gating enabled, unpatched — tokens/sec 94k, queue depth 95th=6, p99=380ms.
3) Gating with async metadata fetch patch (branch: pr/2345) — tokens/sec 108k, queue depth 95th=3, p99=325ms. GPU SM utilization recovered to within 3% of baseline.
4) Gating enabled + eviction-heavy KV-simulation (forced evictions) — reproduced worst-case: tokens/sec 85k, p99 420ms.

Quick triage notes:
- The metadata RPC showed a 99th percentile of ~18ms in prod-catalog, which is small individually but becomes hot-path overhead when synchronized across admission checks.
- KV cache eviction spikes correspond to interleaving pattern; eviction rate correlates with sequence-switch frequency in replay harness.
- The admission check currently holds a mutex for the model shard during validation; making that non-blocking or moving validation off the critical path substantially improves throughput.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short term: merge PR 2345 (async metadata validation) as a canary patch to canary fleet to reduce blocking. Priya to shepherd. Target: canary rollout 2026-11-08.
- Medium term: introduce per-model lightweight admission tokens (non-blocking) and add a soft fallback that serves from the compatible-variant pool when KV cache is being rebuilt. Diego to prototype token-bucket variant by 2026-11-19.
- Observability: add two new probes: 1) per-request admission-block-time (histogram), 2) kv-cache-warmup-duration. Samir to open instrumentation PR and include dashboards.
- Root-cause ticket: JIRA-RINF-7891 created to track the gating serialization root-cause; subtask JIRA-RINF-7897 for metrics/dashboards.

Actionable experiments (owner + timeline):
- Priya: push async metadata validation (PR 2345) to canary, run 48h shadow-run and collect tokens/sec, p95/p99, queue depth. (due 2026-11-08).
- Diego: implement prototype non-blocking admission token bucket and simulated runs with forced KV evictions. Lab target 11-19; initial numbers expected in next weekly sync.
- Samir: add admission-block-time histogram to telemetry, create Grafana dashboard panel and an alert for >5ms median block time at pod level. (due 2026-11-12).
- Tess: craft customer-facing summary explaining transient capacity impact for Dedicated customers who saw slight throughput variance; coordinate with CS if we need outreach. (due 2026-11-09).

Risks / open questions:
- Will the token-bucket approach introduce fairness inversion for low-throughput tenants? Need to simulate multi-tenant fairness scenarios.
- Are there other code paths that synchronously call the model-store metadata RPC? We should search codebase and audit call sites.
- If eviction-heavy workloads are common in certain customers, we might need a pre-warm strategy or a persistent warm-set.

Notes to follow up in the next sync:
- Compare canary metrics after PR 2345 rollout (48h window) vs prior baseline.
- Diego to present prototype numbers for non-blocking admission tokens.
- Samir to present initial dashboard and alert test results.

Referenced runs / artifacts: shadow-run-2026-11-03 (lab replay), ci-load-replay/2026-11-04, pr/2345 branch log. See linked_artifacts for URLs and ticket refs.

Meeting capture ends. This doc is a working record — please add inline notes if you run additional experiments before the next weekly sync.
